name: USWF Championship Tournament: Round One

matches.note: Death won by disqualification when the rest of the stable HC-2000 stormed the ring three-on-one; Mark Williams ran in to clear them out.
Shine won with his finisher, the Shine Line.

notes: Six first-round matches of the fed's own 12-man Championship Tournament; only the two structured here have both combatants minted. The other four (Mark Williams over The Missing Link; Bill Vaughn over Bob Wheeler; Spider over Steely Eyed Don; Justin Credible over Viper, the latter by his own manager Andrea's own mistaken interference) survive in full in the served page's own verbatim text.

name: USWF Championship Tournament: Semi-Finals

matches.note: Shine won after Bill Vaughn ambushed Mark Williams at ringside and passed Shine a pair of brass knuckles.
Spider won by countout after both men brawled outside the ring past the referee's ten-count; Spider then used a baseball bat on the fallen Death.
Steve Shine, having snuck back in unseen, hit Vaughn with the Shine Line; Justin Credible released a submission hold on Vaughn to let Williams make the cover.

notes: The tournament's three semi-final matches, advancing Shine, Spider and Williams to the final triangle match. The source post's own leaked e-mail header block is not reproduced on the served page.

name: USWF Championship Triangle Match

date.source: The fed's own match-history log dates the event 19 April 1998; the broadcast recapping it was posted 20 April.

matches.note: A triangle match for the vacant USWF Championship. Spider was eliminated by countout during a mystery ally's rafters ambush on Death. Chris Williams, introduced minutes earlier as Mark's identical twin, secretly swapped in for his brother and pinned Shine after a distraction from a fallen shoe; the ring announcer credited the win, and the belt, to Mark Williams.

notes: The tournament final. The broadcast itself never clarifies whether Mark or Chris Williams actually wrestled the deciding fall.

name: TV Title Battle Royal

matches.note: A 27-man battle royal for the vacant Television Championship (17 further entrants are unminted here; the full elimination order survives in the served page's own verbatim text). John McKenzie was the last man standing. Steve Shine, who had hidden under the ring for the entire match without ever being eliminated, then ambushed McKenzie after the bell and was declared the new champion by the ring announcer.

notes: 27 wrestlers entered; 10 are minted here. Bill Vaughn was eliminated by Death; Chris Williams was eliminated by Vaughn; Freight and Diesel (Rail Road Express) both competed and were eventually eliminated.

name: MAYhem

date.source: The fed's own 27 April 1998 announcement names 10 May as the date; the title-match recap was posted 11 May.

matches.note: Rail Road Express won the fed's own first Tag Team Championship with their finisher, the Runaway Train, after a ringside brawl drew in a surprise ally, Subway, who immediately joined them in a new stable, Revolution Zero, managed by Sammy.
McKenzie regained the Television Championship after Shine's own manager Krystal Powers's ringside interference backfired.

Vaughn won the USWF Championship after an unidentified masked man attacked Chris Williams (who had Vaughn trapped in a figure-four) at ringside and threw a groggy Mark Williams back into the ring for Vaughn's finisher, the Critical Mass.

notes: The fed's own first pay-per-view; all three of its titles changed hands the same night.
